**Test image observations:**
- Tomato compound leaf with widespread chlorosis (pale yellow-green)
- Multiple brown necrotic spots scattered across leaflets
- One leaflet severely necrotic/dead (left side)
- Brown marginal necrosis on several leaflets
- Dark brown spots with possible lighter centers

Top candidates: Septoria Leaf Blotch (scattered spots, yellowing), Leaf Mold (diffuse yellowing + brown patches).

Using my 1 reference view on Septoria Leaf Blotch:

**Comparison analysis:**
- The Septoria reference shows small, discrete circular spots on otherwise green leaves - this doesn't match the test image well
- The test image has much more extensive/diffuse chlorosis (pale yellow-green throughout) and larger brown areas
- The test image pattern - widespread chlorosis with upper surface browning and progressive necrosis - is more consistent with **Leaf_Mold**, where yellow patches on the upper surface progress to brown/necrotic areas
- Septoria shows small discrete spots (1-4mm) with gray centers on green tissue, which is not what we see here

{"prediction": "Leaf_Mold", "confidence": 0.45, "reasoning": "The test image shows tomato leaflets with diffuse chlorosis (pale yellow-green throughout) and progressive brown necrosis, including severe damage on one leaflet. This pattern of widespread upper-surface yellowing turning to brown is characteristic of Leaf Mold (Fulvia fulva), which causes yellow patches on the upper leaf surface that progress to brown/necrotic areas. The Septoria reference showed small discrete circular spots on green tissue, which did not match. The diffuse chlorosis and large irregular brown areas fit Leaf Mold better than other candidates."}
